sources.entry: nodeScratchpad - Evaluate Nodejs/JS code snippets from Menubar.

summary.one_liner: A native macOS menubar app for evaluating Node.js/JavaScript code snippets in a scratchpad-style editor.
summary.what_it_does: nodeScratchpad is a macOS menubar application that lets you write and evaluate Node.js or JavaScript code snippets. The README describes it as a pure native implementation rather than a cross-platform one. It requires Node.js to be installed and available on the PATH, since snippets are run through it. The README says the editor has syntax highlighting. The roadmap lists planned work on project directory support, configuration management, and inspect options. The README does not describe the evaluation mechanics or editor features in more detail.
use_cases: quickly run small JavaScript snippets on a Mac
evaluate code snippets from the menubar
try out JS expressions without opening a terminal
how_to_run: Make sure Node.js is installed and added to PATH
Download the latest DMG from the releases page
Drag nodeScratchpad.app to the Applications folder
notable: Lives in the macOS menubar for quick access
Pure native macOS implementation, per the README
Syntax highlighting in the snippet editor
Evaluates Node.js/JavaScript snippets using the local Node.js install
caveats: Requires Node.js installed and on PATH
macOS only, as implied by the native implementation and DMG installer
Unsigned builds may trigger an unidentified-developer warning on first launch
